messages:
maria: Hey team, escalating a customer repro — their webhook to /invoke ended up running archive_order instead of cancel_order. Customer expected a refund flow after cancel but order got archived (no refund). Payload attached below.

jon: Oof. Can you paste the exact request body and the response from the router?

maria: Sure — original request body: 
```json
{
  "action": "cancel",
  "order_id": "ord_8f7c9",
  "reason": "customer_requested"
}
```
Router response headers show invoke routed to tool: archive_order v1.2 (score 0.62). User-facing response was a 200 from archive endpoint.

tara: Do we have an autorouter debug trace for that request id? If we can find the scoring features it'd help.

maria: Found it in logs (snipped): 
```
[autorouter] features: { verb_match: 0.9, schema_score: 0.45, alias_overlap: 0.7, recent_success_bias: 0.3 } -> chosen: archive_order (final_score 0.62)
[dispatcher] fallback_rules: none matched
```

jon: Hmm schema_score 0.45 is low — suggests multiple tools matched but archive had higher alias overlap. Do cancel_order and archive_order share similar signatures?

maria: Yes: both accept { order_id, reason } and both have aliases like "cancel", "close", "archive" in their metadata. archive_order also has an optional boolean `permanent` field which customer didn't include.

tara: That alias overlap is bad. We should not rely solely on verb fuzzy match for destructive ops. archive vs cancel are semantically different.

eng-bot: Note: there was a recent model update that increased weight on alias_overlap for faster selection (deployed 2490009000). Could be related.

jon: Repro steps I ran locally: send the same body to /invoke with routing debug on -> got archive_order consistently when alias_overlap weight high. If I flip alias_overlap weight down, cancel_order wins. So confirm it's a scoring weight problem + ambiguous aliases.

maria: Customer impact: order archived; downstream refund job never triggered. They want a rollback and a hotfix.

tara: Immediate mitigation: add a high-priority exact-match rule for tool name tokens when request contains `action: "cancel"`. Also add schema validation to reject if the explicit intent field is missing.

jon: Proposed quick patch: when verb token exactly equals a canonical action in tool metadata, bump its score by +0.5. That should make cancel_order win for exact `cancel`. I'll open a small PR.

maria: Customer asked for a timeline. Can we do a config rollback to previous alias weight first?

eng-bot: Rollback available: weights.yaml@deploy-2489998000. I can trigger a roll back to alias_overlap weight 0.2.

ops-bot: Rolling back alias_overlap weight to 0.2 now (initiated by ops-bot). CI check ok, will deploy to staging then prod after smoke test.

jon: In parallel I'll add the exact-match bump + unit tests that assert cancel payload maps to cancel_order.

maria: For customer rollback, we issued a manual refund and re-opened the order — let support know the manual remediation steps. They asked for a root cause summary and timeframe.

tara: Root cause summary for CS: autorouter scoring favored alias overlap because both tools shared verb aliases; a recent change increased alias weight causing archive_order to win for ambiguous inputs. Fix plan: 1) rollback weight (done), 2) add exact-match scoring bump (PR by jon), 3) tighten tool metadata to remove ambiguous aliases and require explicit `intent` field for archive flows.

jon: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autorouter/pull/324 — adds exact-match bump and new unit tests. Requesting hotfix review.

eng-bot: PR passed CI, merging to hotfix branch. Deploy scheduled to staging in 10m.

ops-bot: Staging smoke passed. Deploying hotfix to prod in 5m. Notifying infra pager.

maria: Customer updated that manual refund went through and they're ok with changes; asked to be informed when hotfix is live.

ops-bot: Hotfix deployed to prod. Canary observed 100 requests: 0 misroutes for cancel payloads.

maria: Thanks all. Follow-ups: we should run a scan for other tools with overlapping aliases (archive, close, cancel, suspend) and create a migration plan to disambiguate. I'll open a ticket in support backlog.

jon: Filed infra ticket INF-4321 and assigned to eng-ml for scoring regression review.

maria: Closing escalation — customer notified and refund confirmed. Will post summary in postmortems channel later. :white_check_mark:
